info.title: Kodi
info.author: MajinGabe
info.description: Media centre - local and network video, music, add-ons
info.details:
Kodi 22 built natively for homebrew Switch consoles (Atmosphère).

This is real Kodi, not a wrapper: its own GUI and renderer, its own audio sink, and the real CPython runtime, so normal Kodi add-ons install and run.

Video: hardware HEVC decode including 10-bit Main 10, software H.264 playback, HLS through inputstream.adaptive, HTTPS with certificate validation.

Input: touch, Joy-Cons and Pro Controller buttons and D-pad. Analog sticks are not wired up yet.

In development: binary add-ons cannot be loaded (only inputstream.adaptive is built in). Exiting from hbmenu takes about 30 seconds because the loader tears the applet down - launched from an NSP forwarder, exit is immediate.

Launch from full-memory hbmenu (hold R on a title) or, better, from a forwarder. Source, build instructions and the development log: https://github.com/MajinGabe/kodi-switch
info.changelog:
v22.0rc2

- fixed a thread-teardown crash during playback (pthread_detach is a stub here)
- 1080p HEVC files are no longer refused before the hardware decoder opens
- the clock shows local time instead of UTC
- System info shows real memory, Atmosphère on Horizon, and battery
- the screenshot action works
- JSON-RPC no longer spins when a connection is aborted

v22.0rc1

First public build.
